title: A part request picked from the Part Library result takes the new number
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Create a part, part A, for this test with 5 on hand.
  • Create a work order for this test, work order 1, with a line holding two part requests, neither ordered nor received: one added by picking part A's "Part Library" result, and one where part A's number was typed by hand and added as typed, with no link to the part.
  • Use a new part number that no part and no Part Library entry has yet, and that does not contain part A's number.
  • Start on the Inventory page (Parts in the top bar, then Inventory in the left menu), on the Active tab.
custom_steps:
1. Type part A's part number in the Search box.
  2. Click the part A row.
  3. Replace the Part Number with the new number.
  4. Click Save.
  5. Click Work Orders in the top bar.
  6. Open work order 1.
  7. Click the Parts tab.
  8. Click Order on the row of the part request picked from the Part Library result.
  9. Click Parts in the top bar.
  10. Click Purchase Orders in the left menu.
  11. Open the newest purchase order.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Part A is listed.

Step 2:

  • Edit Inventory Part opens for part A.

Step 3:

  • Part Number shows the new number.

Step 4:

  • The rename is saved, the window closes and part A's row shows the new number.

Step 5:

  • The Work Orders list opens.

Step 6:

  • Work order 1 opens.

Step 7:

  • The part request picked from the Part Library result reads the new number: it is linked to part A.
  • The part request typed by hand still reads the old number: it only shares the number and has no link to part A.

Step 8:

  • The part request is ordered and goes through.

Step 9:

  • The Parts left menu shows Purchase Orders.

Step 10:

  • The Purchase Orders list opens.

Step 11:

  • The new purchase order's line reads the new number, not the old one.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, version 36 (3 Nov 2026, Chris Ward), read 4 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-10647, story SV-10826 (Story 13, The Part Dialog)

  • S13-R19a: “A line that only shares the old number, typed in by hand with no link to this part, keeps its number. A part request added by picking this part's Part Library result is linked to it, and takes the new number.”
  • S13-R19: “A rename carries over to open work that holds this part, at every location: purchase order lines not yet fully received, part requests not yet received or returned, canned jobs, and returns that are not completed take the new number. A delivery that is not yet accepted is covered by its open purchase order lines. Receiving, ordering, applying a canned job and returning then find the renamed part.”
  • Terminology: “Open work → A purchase order line not yet fully received, a part request not yet received or returned, a canned job, and a return that is not completed.”
